issue_context.title: EndpointSlice controllers should ignore EndpointSlices that are in a terminating state
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

As discussed in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/108267, Endpoint(Slice) controllers can get stuck if an Endpoints or EndpointSlice resource is stuck in a terminating state. 

### What did you expect to happen?

I don't think there's much we can do for Endpoints here since the same name is reused, but EndpointSlice controllers can ignore EndpointSlices in a terminating state.

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/108267

### Anything else we need to know?

_No response_

### Kubernetes version

All supported versions

### Cloud provider

Any

### OS version

Any

### Install tools

Any

Any

Any

@robscott deleting a service with a finalizer doesn't affect the endpointslice, it doesn't change its status to termination or unready

Repro:
1. `kubectl run test --image httpd --port 80`
2. `kubectl expose pod/test`
3. Add finalizer to the service and delete it, it keeps waiting until the finalizer is removed with the deletion timestamp set.
```
$ kubectl get service test -o yaml                                                                                                                                                                             
apiVersion: v1                                                                                                                                                                                                                 
kind: Service                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
metadata:                                                                                                                                                                                                                      
  creationTimestamp: "2022-03-18T09:25:50Z"                                                                                                                                                                                    
  deletionGracePeriodSeconds: 0                                                                                                                                                                                                
  deletionTimestamp: "2022-03-18T09:28:47Z"                                                                                                                                                                                    
  finalizers:                                                                                                                                                                                                                  
  - aojea.io/finalize
```
4. Check the endpoint slice associated
```
kubectl get endpointslices test-kwg96 -o yaml                                                                                                                                                                
addressType: IPv4                                                                                                                                                                                                              
apiVersion: discovery.k8s.io/v1
endpoints:
- addresses:
  - 10.244.0.5
  conditions:
    ready: true
    serving: true
    terminating: false
  nodeName: kind-control-plane
  targetRef:
    kind: Pod
    name: test
    namespace: default
    resourceVersion: "685"
    uid: d84f0db4-469f-4450-9721-8e193b968dab
kind: EndpointSlice
metadata:
  annotations:
    endpoints.kubernetes.io/last-change-trigger-time: "2022-03-18T09:25:50Z"
  creationTimestamp: "2022-03-18T09:25:50Z"
  generateName: test-
  generation: 1
  labels:
    endpointslice.kubernetes.io/managed-by: endpointslice-controller.k8s.io
    kubernetes.io/service-name: test
    run: test
  name: test-kwg96
  namespace: default
  ownerReferences:
  - apiVersion: v1
    blockOwnerDeletion: true
    controller: true
    kind: Service
    name: test
    uid: 405f1291-9b29-4538-a03d-403299d33dda
  resourceVersion: "830"

```


Do you mean that when the endpoint slice controller detects that the Service is being deleted should switch the endpoint slice status to Terminating? cc: @thockin

@aojea I don't think we need to do anything special if the Service is waiting to be deleted. There are many legitimate reasons for this to happen, including waiting for infrastructure to be removed. My main concern with a finalizer was that one on an EndpointSlice could cause the controller to get stuck on a Service. We don't have the same risk with a finalizer on a Service - I don't think that would cause the controller to get stuck in any way.

@robscott @aojea i was unable to repro the issue on my machine:

```
❯ k run test --image httpd --port 80
pod/test created
❯ k expose pod/test
service/test exposed
# add finalizer to endpointslice
❯ k patch endpointslices test-lsxh5 --type json --patch='[ { "op": "add", "path": "/metadata/finalizers", "value": ["kubernetes.io/test"] } ]'
endpointslice.discovery.k8s.io/test-lsxh5 patched
❯ k delete pod test
pod "test" deleted
# deleting the pod, removes the finalizer as reported in the initial issue
❯ k get endpointslices test-lsxh5 -o=jsonpath='{.metadata}'
{"creationTimestamp":"2022-04-19T18:34:17Z","generateName":"test-","generation":6,"labels":{"endpointslice.kubernetes.io/managed-by":"endpointslice-controller.k8s.io","kubernetes.io/service-name":"test","run":"test"},"managedFields":[{"apiVersion":"discovery.k8s.io/v1","fieldsType":"FieldsV1","fieldsV1":{"f:addressType":{},"f:endpoints":{},"f:metadata":{"f:generateName":{},"f:labels":{".":{},"f:endpointslice.kubernetes.io/managed-by":{},"f:kubernetes.io/service-name":{},"f:run":{}},"f:ownerReferences":{".":{},"k:{\"uid\":\"845545f6-0368-4cb8-a8af-8767c634e610\"}":{}}},"f:ports":{}},"manager":"kube-controller-manager","operation":"Update","time":"2022-04-19T18:34:50Z"}],"name":"test-lsxh5","namespace":"default","ownerReferences":[{"apiVersion":"v1","blockOwnerDeletion":true,"controller":true,"kind":"Service","name":"test","uid":"845545f6-0368-4cb8-a8af-8767c634e610"}],"resourceVersion":"2023","uid":"d583f611-b9ad-4c0c-9846-9a18b78d1ebb"}%
# add the finalizer again
❯ k patch endpointslices test-lsxh5 --type json --patch='[ { "op": "add", "path": "/metadata/finalizers", "value": ["kubernetes.io/test"] } ]'
endpointslice.discovery.k8s.io/test-lsxh5 patched
❯ k delete svc test
service "test" deleted
# endpointslice doesn't get deleted because of the finalizer
❯ k get endpointslices
NAME         ADDRESSTYPE   PORTS     ENDPOINTS    AGE
kubernetes   IPv4          6443      172.18.0.2   15m
test-lsxh5   IPv4          <unset>   <unset>      111s
# remove the finalizer
❯ k patch endpointslices test-lsxh5 --type json --patch='[ { "op": "remove", "path": "/metadata/finalizers" } ]'

# removing the finalizer from the endpointslice, triggers the gc and it gets deleted.
❯ k get endpointslices

kubernetes   IPv4          6443    172.18.0.2   17m
```
I was monitoring the logs of `kube-controller-manager`, and the endpointslice controller never complained about `EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date`, when I deleted the service.

Though, I was able to get the controller to log this error under a different scenario. If we don't explicitly remove the finalizer from the endpointslice, and instead re-create the pod and service like:
```
❯ k run test --image httpd --port 80
pod/test created
❯ k expose pod/test
service/test exposed
❯ k get endpointslices
NAME         ADDRESSTYPE   PORTS     ENDPOINTS    AGE
kubernetes   IPv4          6443      172.18.0.2   27m
test-826fs   IPv4          <unset>   <unset>      88s
test-n995d   IPv4          <unset>   <unset>      2m28s
> k logs -f -n kube-system kube-controller-manager-kind-control-plane
W0419 18:46:23.058125       1 endpointslice_controller.go:306] Error syncing endpoint slices for service "default/test", retrying. Error: EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date
W0419 18:46:24.060046       1 endpointslice_controller.go:306] Error syncing endpoint slices for service "default/test", retrying. Error: EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date
W0419 18:46:26.060477       1 endpointslice_controller.go:306] Error syncing endpoint slices for service "default/test", retrying. Error: EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date
W0419 18:46:30.061641       1 endpointslice_controller.go:306] Error syncing endpoint slices for service "default/test", retrying. Error: EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date
W0419 18:46:30.481911       1 endpointslice_controller.go:306] Error syncing endpoint slices for service "default/test", retrying. Error: EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date
W0419 18:46:38.063164       1 endpointslice_controller.go:306] Error syncing endpoint slices for service "default/test", retrying. Error: EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date
W0419 18:47:10.063928       1 endpointslice_controller.go:306] Error syncing endpoint slices for service "default/test", retrying. Error: EndpointSlice informer cache is out of date
```

From what I can understand, because the endpointslice with the finalizer is owned by a service with a different UID than the new endpointslice, it is marked as expected for deletion [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.24.0-beta.0/pkg/controller/util/endpointslice/endpointslice_tracker.go#L154).  The endpointslice controllers calls `endpointsliceTracker.StaleSlices` [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.24.0-beta.0/pkg/controller/endpointslice/endpointslice_controller.go#L367), which returns true for the endpointslice with the finalizer, because of the above reason.

I might be wrong anywhere here, so please let me know if that is the case. As for further action, I'm not sure what can be done here? We could check the endpointslice for finalizers and then skip them [here](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/v1.24.0-beta.0/pkg/controller/util/endpointslice/endpointslice_tracker.go#L102). Keen to hear your thoughts about this.
